s1.syndrome_frame: febrile neutropenia with severe pain and focal lesion in the right arm
salient_findings: severe pain in the right arm radiating to her shoulder
focal cystic necrotic lesion between the teres minor and teres major muscles
key_facts: eczematous plaques on her chest and proximal right arm
splenomegaly 6 cm below the costal margin
coagulase-negative Staphylococcus species in blood cultures
severe pain in the right arm radiating to her shoulder
tender point in the upper lateral scapular region with an underlying vague mass

shortlist.label: Pyomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: severe pain in the right arm and focal lesion on MRI

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: severe pain in the right arm and history of febrile neutropenia

shortlist.label: Invasive fungal infection
shortlist.why_kept: prolonged febrile neutropenia and severe pain

shortlist.label: Bacterial abscess
shortlist.why_kept: severe pain and tender point in the upper lateral scapular region

shortlist.label: Leukemic infiltration
shortlist.why_kept: history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia and severe pain in the right arm

raw.rationale: The patient's severe pain in the right arm radiating to her shoulder, tender point in the upper lateral scapular region with an underlying vague mass, and MRI findings of a focal cystic necrotic lesion between the teres minor and teres major muscles are consistent with pyomyositis, a bacterial infection of the skeletal muscle.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis typically involves bone infection, but the MRI findings in this case show a lesion between muscles, not involving bone.

rejected.label: Invasive fungal infection
rejected.why: The negative serum galactomannan antigen and lack of other evidence of fungal infection make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Bacterial abscess
rejected.why: While the patient has had bacterial infections, the specific location and characteristics of the lesion are more consistent with pyomyositis.

rejected.label: Leukemic infiltration
rejected.why: Leukemic infiltration would not typically cause a focal, painful, and tender mass in the muscle, and the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with an infectious process.
